source.page_title_as_published: Official Latest NFL Injury Report for Players - Week 10 of the 2026 Season | NFL.com
source.week_control: WEEK 10 in the page's own week control; season control 2026; the control listed WEEK 1 through WEEK 10 and 62 seasons

clock.window_evidence: start = the UTC timestamp of this session's claim commit (git); end = when this manifest was written. Individual page reads are ordered in official_reads.json because the fetch harness exposes no per-call clock, so no minute-level per-read timestamp is claimed.
clock.report_day_context: the report covers a Thursday 12 Nov fixture, twelve Sunday 15 Nov fixtures and one Monday 16 Nov fixture; at read time three Sunday games were in progress and two had not kicked off

method.how: all 8 chunks of the live page were read and transcribed row by row into data/availability_snapshot_2026-11-15.csv; the transcription is then machine-checked, not trusted
machine_checks: engine/audit.py re-derives every count (rows, sections, designation coverage, vocabulary) from the CSV, so no number on the site is typed by hand
engine/drift.py pins the expected row count, the required fields and the allowed vocabulary, and fails the build on a missing field or an unexpected value
the row set is diffed against every stored capture of the same page in this repo (6 dated renders), and the diff is published, not hidden
method.caught_by_these_checks: 5 rows were initially mis-parsed (an extra comma on blank-injury rows put practice text into the game-status column); the peer diff caught it and the correction is disclosed in flag RF-14
method.blanks: an empty cell on the official table is stored as an empty string, never as 'None', 'Healthy', or a carried-forward value
method.fields_not_stored_reason: the official report publishes none of them, and the brief forbids inferring them - see governance.json depth_rule

immutability_limitation: the fetch path used here returns a rendered reading of the page, not the page's bytes, so the sha256 values written into data/derived/hashes.json at build time hash this session's stored transcription. They are a transcription fingerprint, not a proof about the original document. A byte-level capture pipeline is SUG-12 option C.
club_coverage: 28 of 32 clubs publish a section; the 4 that do not (CHI, DEN, PHI, TB) are exactly the four clubs in the official schedule page's 'Teams on Bye' block - recomputed at build time in data/derived/capture_audit.json
